passages.c: From a stance of rebellion against traditional architectural design, Ms Ferguson's design for the community pavilion was an astute union of art and nature. Designed as a civilian facility, the pavilion also functioned for the training of battalions from Fort Grieve. Some suggested the design was an attempt to establish dominion over nature. The wider opinion however was that Ms Ferguson had utilised familiar local landmarks for her inspiration. This provided the pavilion with a sense of communion with its natural surroundings.

passages.c: The legends of King Arthur reference a Holy Grail, or an illusive cup with miraculous powers. Legends describe its ability to provide immeasurable happiness, immortality and infinite riches. However, this irresistible desire for happiness, wealth and immortality is not unique to the legends of Arthur. Throughout history and across all cultures we see humanity's impossible desire for more. The alchemists of the ancient cultures pursued the illusive formula that would let them convert common metals into precious gold and make the elixir of immortality. In the story of Aladdin we find a lamp and a genie with the power to grant wishes of immeasurable wealth. These legends sound improbable. Science tells us turning lead into gold is illogical. Yet our stories are full of this irrational quest for the Holy Grail. Novels and films are built around the theme of an irresistible quest for the illusive happiness, riches, fame or immortality.

passages.c: The Transcontinental Race commenced in 2013. It is an annual, endurance cycling event across Europe. The competition covers approximately 4,000 kilometres and requires around ten days to complete. The event is essentially an individual time trial and riders must strategically choose how much time they will devote to riding, resting and refuelling each day. Riders must be unsupported. All food, accommodation and repairs must be purchased from local commercial sources. Riders must therefore undertake careful research to avoid mismanagement of the resources they carry. The race commences in north-western Europe, and riders are required to report at checkpoints before finishing in south-eastern Europe. Riders are required to independently plan their own route and although some ferries are allowed for water crossings, all land based transportation must be undertaken on a bicycle. Riders use mostly paved roads, however routing mistakes or adventurous planning results in some off-road sections. Riders carry a GPS tracker which transmits their position every five minutes. Although the gruelling terrain results in many riders not finishing the race, riders return each year hoping to reduce their times.

passages.c: Nothing could have prepared us for the extraordinary sight from the summit of Mount Everest. In all directions jaggered peaks rose from the earth seeming to proclaim the majesty of nature. Our progress up the mountain had been complicated by a howling storm, but the dream of the summit had propelled us forward. Now here we stood in awe, and everything else had become extraneous. Unexpectedly, the wind shifted directions and dark clouds began to roll across the sky. It is difficult to describe the fear that knifed through our hearts at the sight of the imminent weather. These emotions we had to defeat if we had any chance of surviving the challenging descent.

passages.c: Considerable historical evidence suggests that herbs and spices have long been used for their health and medicinal benefits. Although the ancient civilisations appear quite knowledgeable about the benefits of herbs and spices, they did not distinguish between those used for flavouring or medicinal purposes. If the leaves, seeds, roots or gums had an agreeable taste or odour, they became the norm for use in that culture. During the middle ages, food preservation methods were limited, so perishable foods were difficult to store. To disguise the horrible flavours and odours of foods that were going sour, strong spices were used. The rich flavours of the spices made the food much more edible. Initially spices were expensive and unavailable to the rural peasants. However, as exploration and trade with Asia progressed, new oriental spices became available. Spices were also valuable items of trade and fashionable signs of wealth.

passages.c: Marie Curie was an astute physicist and chemist who conducted influential research on radioactivity. She was an intelligent woman, becoming the first female to be awarded a Nobel Prize. Her talent was further recognised when she became the first person, and only woman, to accomplish this twice. Her commitment to science is reflected in the fact that she is the only person to win a Nobel Prize in two dissimilar sciences. Marie was a Polish emigrant who relocated to Paris where she completed her university education and conducted her subsequent scientific experiments. Her most reputable achievements include the development of the theory of radioactivity and the discovery of two radioactive elements. Marie is credited with the establishment of several centres of medical research. During World War 1, she developed mobile radiography units for field hospitals to improve the treatment of patients using X-ray services.

passages.c: A constitutional crisis arose across the British Empire in 1936. King Edward VIII expressed his tenacious desire to marry the notorious socialite and divorcee Wallis Simpson. Wallis had divorced her first husband and was in the process of divorcing her second. The royal establishment opposed the union articulating various legal, political, religious and moral objections. Most serious was the belief that Wallis Simpson was politically and socially unsuitable as a prospect for a queen consort and they were suspicious she was more interested in the associated fame and fortune. King Edward VIII was unable to negotiate his intention and seemed oblivious to the concerns of the establishment. The ambitious Simpson continued to fascinate Edward which led to his decision to abdicate the throne in 1936. Edward was succeeded by his cautious brother Albert, who reigned as King George VI.

passages.c: Our modern world has become obsessed with the artificial. We are not satisfied with the beauty of residential gardens with their rolling lawns. We have embraced instead artificial lawns, with their potential to preserve us time for other pursuits. Our preoccupation with social media is also an obsession with the artificial. Facebook friends are no substitute for a friendship forged by time spent together in confidential conversation and common pursuits. Are these artificial options beneficial to our health as a society? Do they lack the crucial elements essential for human happiness?

passages.c: The table was prepared with excruciating attention to detail and was dressed with embroidered chiffon cloths. Vases of vibrant fuchsia graced the tables. At each extremity of the table a silver tray was arranged with exotic fruits surrounding an intricately carved watermelon of an oceanic scene. A tower of champagne glasses, delicately balanced, formed the centrepiece of the table. Above the table a crystal chandelier was suspended. Its shimmering light reflected in the polished floors. The soothing notes of a concerto completed the peaceful and spectacular scene. Suddenly, a child's laugh ricocheted across the room as a flash of colour and energy dove beneath the table. The chef, a large burly man, appeared from the kitchen. His moustache twitched as his eyes scanned the room. Spying the child tucked beneath the chaise lounge, he reached to drag him out. But to his chagrin, the child slipped through his grasp and out the door.

passages.c: During the reign of a foreign sovereign, a gnome was assigned the task of designing a garden for the monarch. The design was part of the sovereign's campaign to foster the approval of the people. In choosing the gnome for the task, he wished to align himself with those who would support his reign. The monarch arranged a consignment of jewels to be delivered to the gnome, however the consignment was delivered instead to an evil gnat. Unwilling to return such a treasure, the gnat gnawed through the gnarled wooden box containing the jewels and kept the jewels for himself. As the assigned time of the champagne breakfast to celebrate the opening of the new garden approached, the gnome was forced to erect a sign carved from a gnarled old tree but with no jewels to adorn it.

passages.c: To be honest, winning a scholarship to study in Africa was not exactly the reward I had imagined. The honour of photographing the rhinoceros for the natural history exhibition sounded glamorous, but the reality was ghastly. Upon arriving in Africa, after hours in transit, I was exhausted. The vehicle sent to the airport appeared to have come straight from the local ghetto and I wondered if it was reliable. The ancient schooner, which was to take me into the heart of the African wilderness was no larger than a dinghy. It was adapted to river exploration with a small outboard motor but the captain refused to keep the sails furled. They flapped aimlessly in the breeze, and at night resembled ghosts against the dark African sky. Supplies were safely stacked in crates, but living on salty gherkins and tinned spaghetti left a person hankering for a home cooked meal. Despite the difficult living conditions, the trip resulted in the most exhilarating experience of my life. At dusk we heard the rhythm of hooves across the plains. Then on the horizon the silhouette of a black rhinoceros herd. It was a thrill to photograph this amazing animal and hopefully raise awareness before it is annihilated.

passages.c: The elderly man scrutinized the barren cupboard. Once this had been like a food depot laden with delicious treats. He could almost taste the raspberry nougat his wife regularly prepared and the camembert they purchased from the local farmers' market. But a memory was all that remained. His heart leapt at the sight of a white ball in the back corner of the cupboard. Reaching his frail hand, he eagerly grabbed it only to discover it was a receipt. His shoulders slumped. How had it come to this? From his debut on the stage he had developed a rapport with his audiences that earned him fame and success. But now he was elderly and unable to pay his mortgage. A terrible cough racked his body. The pneumonia had returned. Shuffling towards the door he muttered his favourite psalm. He urgently needed assistance.

passages.c: Through a sinkhole deep in the forest of south-eastern Europe is a subterranean world of underground amphitheatres and narrow passages. This is the home of the rare and unusual olm. Although the olm is a species of salamander, unlike other amphibians it spends its entire life submerged in the waterways. The olm is specifically adapted for the dark life in a cave. Despite its substandard eye sight, its other senses are well developed. It has no skin colour and can survive for years subsisting on little or no food. A subspecies of olm has been discovered in the caves of Slovenia, however these have black skin and functioning eyes. In the lakes of Mexico another unusual amphibian can be found. The axolotl, or Mexican walking fish, lives submerged in water. If the axolotl is subject to injury and looses a limb, it can regenerate and replace the limb. Burrowed in the subsoil of the Arctic Circle is another unusual place to find an amphibian. Here the wood frog can survive subzero temperatures with most of its body frozen. The frog exists in this winter hibernation for weeks with its heart and breathing suspended. These unusual amphibians have submitted to their harsh environments and survived!

passages.c: Pride and Prejudice, a novel by Jane Austen, is a witty critique of the lives of the upper classes in Regency England. The novel revolves around the preface that one should marry for love and not the prevailing belief of the time that a wealthy match was essential. Mr Bennet has five daughters, all of whom are prevented from inheriting his estate. His wife's preoccupation with securing husbands for her daughters is therefore central to the story. However, the story expresses a precaution for those who rush into hasty marriages and find themselves disappointed. The eldest daughters, Jane and Elizabeth, whose prerequisite for marriage is love and respect, ultimately find their happiness. Pride and Prejudice continues to fascinate modern readers and is as appreciated today as in previous generations. It is Austen's memorable characters that have formed the basis of numerous dramatic adaptations which aim to imitate this remarkable novel.

passages.c: The landing at ANZAC Cove was a part of the invasion of Gallipoli, and aimed to displace the control of the Turks over the peninsula. Although they were positioned ashore north of their intended landing, the troops never disobeyed orders. The ANZAC troops disembarked under cover of night. In the darkness the assault formations became disorganised but the troops gradually made their way inland. Soon after coming ashore, the ANZAC plans were discarded and the battalions were thrown into battle without clear orders. With disbelief the soldiers realised their position at the base of steep cliffs put them at great disadvantage with the Turks firing from above. However, with brave disregard for their own safety, the soldiers clung to the cliff faces and formed a beachhead. Dissatisfied with the safety of their troops, the ANZAC commanders requested an evacuation. However, there was disagreement about the practicality of the evacuation and so the soldiers fought on. Over two thousand men lost their lives that day. These men came to represent mateship, honour and a survival spirit in the face of great discomfort.

passages.c: Arnold Viceroy began his career at a local interschool athletics competition. A last minute change of competitors saw him compete in the high jump event where he convincingly leapt to the lead. Arnold's performance attracted the interest of the vice-president of the Athletic Association and he was offered the opportunity to compete at an interstate level. Within weeks Arnold had launched to the top of the national record board. After graduation and a brief interlude to pursue travel dreams, Arnold returned to athletics and was appointed vice-captain of the national athletics team. His career was interrupted after sustaining a serious knee injury when intercepting a football in a social game. However, Arnold's determination to return to international competition paid off. After an interval of intense therapy he returned to place first in men's high jump at an international competition. In a recent interview, Arnold described his retirement from international athletics as a chance to pursue a new dream. Helping young people to discover their talents and reach their potential will be his focus in his new appointment as vice-principal.

passages.c: A retrospective analysis of the space shuttle disaster revealed obvious flaws in both the design and management of the launch. The findings indicated the retrorockets were installed incorrectly resulting in an acceleration rather than deceleration of the shuttle. The absence of retrofire rockets further obstructed the shuttle's ability to manoeuvre as required. Interviews with control staff revealed concerns regarding the leadership of General Kirk, the commander of the mission. The General was described as an obstinate man who would not consider the concerns of the technical staff. Determined there would be no obstacle in the launch of the shuttle, he failed to investigate the engineer's concerns regarding the retrofit of the new technology. The investigation found General Kirk was negligent. As commander he was obligated to pursue all reports of technical faults. As a result there will be a retrospective investigation of all missions under the command of General Kirk.

passages.c: Alexander Fleming discovered the mould penicillium and its antibacterial properties. During the next 20 years scientists discovered how to purify and even produce synthetic antibiotics. These became widely used in medicine as they were beneficial in treating infections. Even in ancient cultures, humans recognised the powerful antiseptic properties of natural substances. Moulds were used in ancient Egypt to treat infections. Garlic and honey have long been used in many cultures due to their beneficial antiseptic and antibacterial properties. But without medicines or other remedies, how does the human body fight disease? When an antigen, such as bacteria or other toxin, enters our body, our immune system produces antibodies. These antibodies allow our body to recognise and destroy the invading bacteria or virus. Nature's ability to produce antibodies is also used in the production of antidotes to venomous animals. A small amount of the toxic venom is injected into an animal and then the resulting antibodies are extracted from the host's blood. The result is a powerful antivenom.

These impressive limestone towers stand resistant to the abrasion which shapes the sand dunes, and yet this somewhat aberrant fact baffles scientists. One theory suggests that trees absorbed the hard calcrete dissolved in underground water. The hypothesis is that the tree casts became buried by sands only to become exposed again with the abrasion of the winds. At first glance it seems all life is absent from this sandy desert landscape. However, this area is an abode for a surprising number of animals including kangaroos, emus, carpet pythons, sand goannas and black cockatoos. Although it is tempting, visitors must abstain from climbing on the unique pinnacle structures if they are to be preserved for future generations to enjoy.

passages.c: In an age when thoughts of nationalism permeated Australian hearts, the federation movement began. Henry Parkes is perceived as the 'Father of Federation' and a founding father of Australia. An autodidact from a working class family, Parkes became one of the most commanding figures in Australian politics. He was an articulate and powerful proponent of Australia's federation and increasing autonomy from Great Britain. Despite early opposition, he persevered and changed the individual colonial states perspective to one of nationalism. Andrew Clark, principal author of the Australian Constitution, is another founding father whose belief in the need for social reforms pervaded his draft of the constitution. During his extended political career he fought for Australian independence, for an autonomous judiciary, and for fair electoral practices including the rights of women to vote. Edmund Barton served as the first Prime Minister of a newly autonomous Australia. He contributed to the federation movement, perceiving the need for free trade and movement between the colonies of Australia. He also fought for both the lower and upper houses to be a representative government. These men opposed autocratic leadership and fought for the freedoms on which our nation was built.

Ace turned the space ship toward the mighty asteroid looming on a collision course for Earth. It was imperative they got the coordinates exact, or the consequences could be catastrophic. Ace glanced out the side window and observed the other vessels, all with instructions to converge on that looming rock. With the combined impact of the rockets, they were ordered to discharge and alter the course of the asteroid. But it was a complicated manoeuvre. If they detonated too early, the rockets may not connect with the asteroid. If they detonated too late, the vessel itself may collide with the asteroid. Ace knew such a collision would mean more than a mild concussion. With one last glance at his companion, Ace nodded. It was time.

passages.c: My Nana resides in the yellow section of a semi-detached townhouse. My brothers and I lodge with her on a semi-permanent basis. I suppose we have come to consider her home with the peeling, semi-gloss, yellow paint as our residence too. Maybe more so than the crowded box we used to live in on the base, squished between all the other boxes on the street that resembled a semi-circle. Nana's house has an air of mystery and adventure. In that semi-conscious state before sleep claims me at night, I can hear strange noises from the dwelling next door. I often dream of what would happen if I discovered the secret door that connected the two halves of the semi-detached dwelling Nana calls home. Then one day, I discovered it. Well not a door exactly, but a gate. Hidden beneath the wild rose in the backyard was a little hemisphere shaped gate that lead next door. What I discovered on the other side was not the adventure I expected, but maybe better. Johnny inhabits the house next door. He is a hemiplegic due to an accident. That strange noise I could hear was Johnny practicing wheelchair basketball. He is in the semi-final next week and I am his new greatest fan.

passages.c: Years of war and excessive spending had left the monarchy enveloped in debt. However, King Louis XVI's decision to increase taxes emblazed the anger of the French people. With the storming of the Bastille, the people embarked on a revolution which would reshape their nation and the world. The French citizens envisioned a different future, free of an absolute monarch. Free of the feudal system which seemed to enclose their lives and remove their freedom. Many citizens embraced the new ideology, but they were soon to discover a darker side. During the reign of terror, thousands of French citizens were executed for anti-revolutionary activities. Their crime was holding beliefs contrary to the Jacobin government. It was during this period that the image of the guillotine came to encapsulate the French Revolution. The entrance of a young Napoleon led to the end of the French Revolution and the beginning of a dictatorship. However to this day, the French Revolution embodies the power inherent in the will of the people.

passages.c: Society's paradigm of the malnourished person consists of an emaciated skeleton. However, the paradox of a malnourished obese person is a serious health concern. Around the world today, millions of people suffer from malnutrition. For many it is the result of poverty, drought and a lack of food. For others an intestinal parasite steals their nutrients. But even in the apparent paradise of the western world with our overflowing supermarkets, malnutrition results in poor health. Our abundance is only superficial when we consider the nutritional value of the foods we consume. Not all foods are superior sources of nutrients and energy. Processed sugars and starches are superfluous, with no nutritional value. In addition, malabsorption disorders result in a person lacking vital nutrients despite having consumed healthy food. If any of the steps involved in digestion malfunctions, intestinal malabsorption may occur.

passages.c: The Taiga forest accounts for an astounding 29% of the world's forest cover. This evergreen forest extends across northern Europe, Asia and America making it the largest terrestrial biome on earth. With a harsh climate and most precipitation falling as snow through the long winters, the forest is extremely dry. Some lichens and mosses grow here, but most of the vegetation is coniferous trees. These trees have some marvellous features which allow them to survive. They have long, thin, waxy needles which can survive the cold and they don't loose their leaves like the deciduous trees, allowing them to make the most of photosynthesis in the brief summer. It takes a courageous animal to survive the harsh winters in the Taiga, but the animals that inhabit this forest have certain characteristics that are advantageous for survival. Animals include carnivorous predators, such as wolves, bears and foxes, numerous birds and herbivores such as rabbits, squirrels, moose and deer. During the winters, some animals hibernate, others migrate and others face the dangerous cold in thick fur coats. In summertime, the bogs and ponds of the Taiga become a breeding place for numerous insects and migratory birds.

Her shoulders slumped as the memories came flooding back. What a spectacle she had made arguing for the truth as the man she quoted publicly denied ever speaking with her. As she slumped in her tiny cubicle, loneliness began to wrap its tentacles around her broken heart. Alone she would have to face the consequences and it would be a miracle if her career survived. It was then that fear crept in like icicles forming and she felt her whole world begin to freeze. How would she approach tomorrow?

passages.c: The Sydney Olympic Games of 2000 were a celebration of Olympic values and athletic excellence. Patriotic athletes from 199 countries proudly displayed their flags in the parade of nations. The historic first Olympics of a new century celebrated 100 years of women's participation in the games. Australia presented a dramatic opening ceremony. It included acts symbolic of Australia's historic past including stock horses, the first fleet and a parade of lawnmowers and Hills Hoist clotheslines. A majestic dance by indigenous women cleansed and protected the games. After the lengthiest Olympic torch relay, extending 100 days around Australia, Cathy Freeman lit the gigantic Olympic torch. Ten days later she won the 400m final in front of an enthusiastic crowd. The Australian team won an impressive 58 medals earning the pride of the Australian public.

The pair realised they were in grave danger. The distress signal was received by NSW police and a rescue vessel was mobilised. Treacherous seas threatened to jeopardise the rescue. Prior to sunrise on Tuesday morning, the rescue vessel sighted the stranded sailors. Both men expressed their relief that the rescue occurred efficiently in such hostile conditions. "We wish to recognise the bravery of those who travelled to our aid," Mr Kent announced. The pair reported waves the size of buildings had terrorised them during the night as they clung to the yacht. They could not disguise their relief. "Horrid seas like that tend to paralyse a man in fear," Mr Kent admitted. Both men were hospitalised for exposure and dehydration but are otherwise recovering well.
